Position Summary:
At CVS Health, we are focused on transforming health care for our customers and making our company a great place to work. We help people navigate the health care system – and their personal health care – by improving access, lowering costs and being a trusted partner for every meaningful moment of health. Within our Retail locations, we bring this promise to life with heart every day. Our 3rd year Pharmacy Interns play a critical role in supporting our pharmacy teams to consistently deliver on our brand promise, while developing their own skills in preparation for increasing responsibility.
As a 3rd year Pharmacy Intern, you will be focused on applying didactic learning from pharmacy school into real-world practice to become ready for a Pharmacist role. Under the direction of your preceptor, you will complete a comprehensive training roadmap designed to show you first-hand what it’s like to be part of a pharmacy team while gaining an overview of store, district, and regional operations. You will gain valuable hands-on experience through a training roadmap that includes a combination of Key Learning Experiences (KLEs), activities, and time spent with leaders in your district. While in the pharmacy, you will assist the pharmacy team to ensure that pharmacy operations run smoothly, our patients’ prescriptions are filled promptly, safely, and accurately, and we are providing caring service that exceeds patient expectations. You will learn to operate as part of the pharmacy team through consistent application of Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), best practices, and effective communication. Throughout your shifts and in all customer and colleague interactions, you will learn to demonstrate empathy and genuine care, and contribute to a safe and inclusive culture where all people feel valued and empowered.
3rd year Pharmacy Interns are responsible for completion of a comprehensive training roadmap, focusing on KLEs that build aptitude in the following areas. As tenure increases, 3rd year Pharmacy Interns take on increasing responsibility of the safety and effectiveness of operations in the pharmacy, including but not limited to:
Living our purpose by following all company SOPs at each workstation to help our Pharmacists and Technicians manage and improve patient health
Following pharmacy workflow procedures at each pharmacy workstation (i.e., production, pick-up, drive-thru, and drop-off) for safe and accurate prescription fulfillment

Job Title:
Manufacturing Production Documentation Co-Op
Job Description:
Here at Entegris, we use advanced science to enable technologies that transform the world, and we are seeking employees who have the drive to continue the mission.
The Role:
Our site in Chaska, MN is seeking a Manufacturing Production Documentation Co-Op to join our team for the Spring 2027 season. This assignment is intended to be 6 months in duration.
This role will be focused on improving, standardizing, and aligning manufacturing documentation—especially for injection molding processes. You will work closely with cross‑functional teams (quality, molding, machining, operators) to identify gaps, resolve inconsistencies, and update technical documents such as SOPs, work instructions, mold setup sheets, process parameter records, and validation protocols. The role blends technical writing, process understanding, and operator-focused clarity, helping ensure documentation is accurate, consistent, and easy for production teams to use.
What You’ll Do:
Document Review — They audit existing molding documents (SOPs, work instructions, setup sheets, process parameters) to find outdated, unclear, or inconsistent content.
Process Mapping — They observe molding operations on the floor, map out steps, and ensure documentation matches real‑world practice.
Template Standardization — They help build or refine templates, so all documents look and read the same across molding, machining, and quality.
Cross‑Functional Collaboration — They work with engineers, technicians, operators, and quality teams to clarify instructions and resolve discrepancies.
Mold Setup Documentation — They update mold setup sheets, ensuring correct part numbers, tooling, parameters, and photos are included.
Process Parameter Alignment — They verify that documented molding parameters match validated settings and update records when needed.
Operator‑Friendly Simplification — They rewrite complex technical language into clear, step‑by‑step instructions operators can easily follow.
Part Family Organization — They help group similar molded parts and align documentation across families to reduce redundancy.
Pilot Testing — They test new documentation formats with operators, gather feedback, and refine the templates.
Quality & Compliance Support — They ensure documents meet internal standards, regulatory requirements, and audit expectations.
What We Seek:
Technical writing — Ability to write clear, structured, operator‑friendly documentation.
Manufacturing process knowledge — Basic understanding of injection molding or willingness to learn quickly.
Software proficiency — Comfortable with Microsoft Word, Excel, PowerPoint; familiarity with Visio or flowcharting tools is a plus.
CAD exposure — Experience with SolidWorks or AutoCAD is beneficial but not always required.
Attention to detail — Critical for reviewing and correcting technical documents.
Communication skills — Ability to work with engineers, technicians, operators, and quality teams.
Organization — Managing multiple documents, part families, and revision histories.
Problem‑solving — Identifying inconsistencies and proposing improvements.
Desired Major(s) & Graduation Year:
Mechanical Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Industrial Engineering, Chemical Engineering
Graduating in 2027 or 2028
Eligibility:
Must be a currently enrolled student
Available to work 40 hours a week, M-F (8a-5p) beginning in January through June
Must be familiar with the university’s requirements to participate in a co-op program
Entegris is not currently hiring candidates for co-ops/internships who will need, now or at any time in the future, Entegris sponsorship through the H1-B lottery.
PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS:
The following physical requirements will be Machine‑area mobility, wearing PPE while on the plant floor, attention to detail, light lifting (up to 30 lbs), along with standing and walking.
WHY WORK AT ENTEGRIS?
Lead. Inspire. Innovate. Define Your Future. 
Not everyone who works for a global company shares the same background, experiences and perspectives. We leverage the differences of our employees to bring new ideas to the table. Every employee throughout the company is encouraged to share input on projects and initiatives. Our decision-making process is truly a collaborative effort as we realize there are leaders at every level of the organization. We put our values at the core of how we operate as an organization — not just when it’s convenient, but in a lasting and meaningful way. We want the time and energy you spend here to have a positive impact on your life inside and outside of the office.

Our total rewards package goes above and beyond just a paycheck. Whether you’re looking to build your career, improve your health, or protect your wealth, we offer generous benefits to help you achieve your goals.

Job Description
Kickstart Your Career at Vertex! 
Are you ready to make a real impact? At Vertex, our mission is to tackle serious diseases and to change lives, for the better, for the future. Our aim is to give you the skills, insights, and career guidance to be an important part of that future; to turn your potential into progression. As a Vertex intern or co-op, you’ll work on meaningful projects, collaborate with talented teams, and learn from industry leaders. We’re passionate about innovation, inclusion, and supporting your growth—inside and outside the lab. 
Why Vertex? 
Real Projects: You’ll work on assignments that make a real impact, not just busy work.

Inclusive Culture: Collaboration and inclusion are embedded in everything we do. 
Career Launchpad: Build skills, explore career paths, and get guidance for your future career. 
Your Impact
The Vertex Predictive Models Co-Op is a 6-month experiential training program for students currently working towards an advanced degree in Biological Sciences, or other related fields. If you are passionate, collaborative, and growth-minded, a co-op at Vertex will help you gain meaningful experience in our Analytical Development functional areas and serve as a launchpad for your career.
The application deadline for this co-op is November 15th. Please note that Vertex reviews applications on a rolling basis and reserves the right to close this job posting prior to the listed deadline. Applicants can expect to receive an update about their application before or shortly after the application deadline.
Ready to apply? Submit your application and let’s turn possibilities into reality! 
 What you will be doing: 
The Co-op will support the development of predictive in vitro assays designed to identify factors associated with successful islet engraftment, graft resilience, and in vivo performance. This role offers hands-on experience in cell-based assay development, functional characterization of islet systems, and translational biomarker research.
Working as part of a collaborative research team, the Co-op will evaluate islet systems under transplantation-relevant stress conditions—including oxidative stress, serum exposure, cytokines, and other challenges that model the implantation environment. The successful candidate will contribute to experimental execution, data analysis, scientific documentation, and communication of findings to the project team.
Key Responsibilities:
Support the design, planning, and execution of in vitro studies using islet-based systems.
Perform cell-based assays to evaluate:Cell viability
Functional performance
Stress responses
Biomarker profiles
Evaluate transplantation-relevant stress conditions, such as oxidative stress, serum exposure, cytokine challenge, and related implantation-environment models.
Assist in identifying assay readouts that may correlate with engraftment, graft resilience, and in vivo outcome.
Analyze, interpret, and summarize experimental data using appropriate scientific and analytical methods.
Maintain accurate, timely, and well-organized experimental records, including methods, raw data, observations, and conclusions.
Communicate study progress, results, and recommendations clearly to project team members.
Prepare a final presentation and/or written project summary outlining findings, conclusions, and proposed next steps.
Collaborate effectively with cross-functional colleagues while independently managing assigned experimental activities.
Qualifications:
Advanced Degree (Master's/PhD)
Basic laboratory experience with cell-based assays and/or mammalian cell culture.
Strong organizational, analytical, and scientific documentation skills.
Ability to interpret experimental data and communicate results clearly, both verbally and in writing.
Ability to work effectively both independently and as part of a collaborative team.
Detail-oriented approach to experimental execution, data recording, and quality of work.
Familiarity with assays related to:Cell viability
Cellular function
Stressing culture
Biomarker
Interest in translational research, assay development, and cell therapy or regenerative medicine
Legal authorization to work in the United States, now and in the future. Please note that Vertex does not provide sponsorship for internships/co-ops or entry level roles within this part of the organization.
